HOW_TO_READ_LOGS.txt.content:
================================================================================
          OSIRIS SECOPS FIELD MANUAL // HOW TO READ SYSTEM LOGS
================================================================================
Alice — when an attack happens, system daemons log events to /var/log/.
Raw logs look dense, but every line follows a strict 4-part anatomy:

  [ TIMESTAMP ]  [ HOST ]  [ DAEMON/SERVICE ]   [ EVENT MESSAGE ]
  03:38:10       osiris    sshd[204]:           Invalid user operator from 192.168.1.105
  └── When       └── Where └── Who logged it    └── What actually happened

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. THE 4 COMMON INCIDENT DAEMONS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• 'sshd[PID]'   : Secure Shell logins (brute force attacks, unauthorized entry).
• 'sudo'        : Administrator privilege escalation.
• 'kernel'      : Core OS hardware & network link events.
• 'systemd[1]'  : System service supervisor (terminated daemons).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. YOUR LOG INVESTIGATION TOOLKIT:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• [1;33mcat <file>[0m            : Stream an entire log from start to finish.
• [1;33mhead -n 5 <file>[0m      : Peek at the earliest events (e.g. system boot).
• [1;33mtail -n 10 <file>[0m     : Focus on the latest events (e.g. recent attack activity).
• [1;33mgrep -i "pattern" <file>[0m: Filter the noise to isolate specific keywords or alerts.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. TRIAGE VERIFICATION:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Read 'REPAIR_COMMANDS.txt' for the list of triage verification commands to
register confirmed security leads into your incident dossier.
================================================================================

           SYSADMIN CHEAT SHEET // PRACTICAL 'grep' LOG FORENSICS
================================================================================
When triaging system breaches, raw logs contain hundreds of noisy events.
Use 'grep' recipes to isolate critical incident keywords:

1. ISOLATE ALERTS & ERRORS (Case-Insensitive):
   • [1;33mgrep -i 'alert' /var/log/auth.log[0m
   • [1;33mgrep -i 'alert' /var/log/syslog[0m
   • [1;33mgrep -i 'error' /var/log/syslog[0m

2. FILTER RUNAWAY PROCESSES & HARDWARE LINKS:
   • [1;33mgrep -i 'miner' /var/log/auth.log[0m
   • [1;33mgrep -i 'osiris0' /var/log/syslog[0m

3. SHOW LINE NUMBERS & EXCLUDE NOISY DAEMONS:
   • [1;33mgrep -n -i 'failed' /var/log/auth.log[0m   (Show line numbers)
   • [1;33mgrep -v 'systemd' /var/log/syslog[0m      (Invert match: strip daemon noise)
================================================================================
